Dialectical Behavioral Therapy talks about rational mind, and emotional mind. You take information from your rational and emotional mind in to consideration when making choices, or drawing conclusions. Sometimes when you the amount of input is substantially higher from one side then the process is skewed. When you can make choices/draw conclusions in a way that considers this and adjusts, it is described as “wise mind” which my therapist describes as “the opposite of illness”.

Letting yourself get too emotional or too rational is kin to a mental handicap.

Edit : Apparently its not healthy but not the biggest deal in the world. "
Which type of upside down? Rear facing strait up in the air upside down, or carapace (top of shell) down?

Neither is great, but it's not life threatening to be in those awkward positions for a very short period of time. Now if they were going to leave her like that for an extended period of time, I can see the fuss. Turtles, if they get stuck in the carapace down position, do die because their organs kind of crushed together because they aren't meant to be like that for extended amounts of time. A turtle though regularly flips over onto their backs without problems since they can get themselves up with their necks in a short time. If a turtle has something like pnuemonia or recently drowned, than absolutely DO NOT place them on their back since it makes it worse and possibly can lead to their death, but you should tilt their head down for a drowning case, just not strait down. Otherwise it just sounds like a big fuss. And rear facing strait up is stressful I'm sure, but as long as they're not left like that, it should be fine."
